“The Internet before Big Data had real outlaws and hackers. The punks were computer scientists, programmers, citizens, advocates and working professionals who built tools to resist. “

We were also people who cared about things other than our egos, ambitions, and profits. We were trying — sometimes successfully, sometimes not — to make the world a better place for everyone, not just for ourselves. Those of us who grew up with the Cold War and the civil rights struggles and the birth of the environmental movement and the Vietnam War and all the tumult of the 1960’s saw the possibility for a better world, moreover, we saw the necessity of a better world. And we tried to build part of it, using the tools at our disposal.

We could still have that better world…but it won’t arrive peacefully. The window in which that was possible has closed, and now — sadly — it will have to come via other means. As an aging peace-love-flowers-music hippie I hate that it’s come to this; but the realist in me knows there’s no other way, and it is the people standing in the way of that world who have themselves created this situation.
